source.documentTitle: Curriculum and Assessment Policy Statement: Mathematics Grades 4–6
source.authorityNote: Official DBE CAPS subject document. Its cover/copyright information identifies the document as a 2011 publication. Confirm current amendments and policy status before treating this seed as production-authoritative.

skills: Addition and subtraction facts involving units and multiples of 10, 100 and 1 000
Multiplication of whole numbers to at least 12 × 12
Multiplication facts involving units and tens by multiples of 10, 100, 1 000 and 100 000
Order, compare and represent numbers up to at least 9-digit numbers
Represent prime numbers to at least 100
Recognise place value in whole numbers up to at least 9-digit numbers
Round off to the nearest 5, 10, 100 and 1 000
Use estimation and a range of written and mental calculation techniques to perform and check calculations
teachingGuidance: Develop mental Mathematics systematically rather than using random daily calculations.
Integrate mental Mathematics with concepts and techniques taught in the main lesson.
Keep number ranges lower in Term 1 and increase them during the year.
At the start of the year, number ranges and techniques may be based on Grade 5 learning.

sourceRefs.section: 3.3.3 Clarification of content for Grade 6 — Grade 6 Term 1

records.mappingNote: These are extracted topic-level skills and teaching notes, not a complete assessment rubric or a fully decomposed list of individual learning objectives.

records.topic: 1.1 Whole numbers — counting, ordering, representing and place value of digits
skills: Order, compare and represent numbers up to at least 9-digit numbers
Represent prime numbers to at least 100
Recognise place value of digits in whole numbers up to at least 9-digit numbers
Round off to the nearest 5, 10, 100 and 1 000
prerequisiteAndProgressionNotes: Learners should be proficient in Grade 5-level counting.
Term 1 should revise and consolidate work from Grade 5.
Counting should use varied representations and apparatus, not only verbal counting.
Place-value representations include number names, place-value or flash cards, and expanded notation.
suggestedTeachingApparatus: Structured, semi-structured and empty number lines
records.mappingNote: The CAPS clarification notes include a narrower place-value range in one explanatory paragraph while the stated skill outcome specifies up to at least 9-digit numbers. Preserve both statements and flag for specialist interpretation rather than silently reconciling them.

skills: Write number sentences to describe problem situations
Solve and complete number sentences by inspection
Solve and complete number sentences by trial and improvement
teachingGuidance: Use number sentences as preparation for writing algebraic equations.
Connect number sentences with verbal problems, diagrams and flow diagrams.
Use equivalent statements to build understanding of calculation steps.
Use number sentences to support multiple operations with and without brackets and the order of operations.
